standing: ASSESSMENT ONLY. No source edited, no implementation produced, no commit/push/publication.
question: Does the published deterministic evaluator contract fully define the join from policy DSL subject enumeration and filters to retained native fact/scope/Coverage/import records, such that an independent implementer reconstructs the same subjects, matching facts, completeness, findings and verdict without inventing public semantics?

verdict.summary: The join is substantially built but not closed. Nine public semantics are unpublished; four are central to the asked question. Each is demonstrated by two conforming readings that produce different retained proof2 bytes from one Plan.
verdict.gapClass: missing public selection semantics, not missing retention and not implementation freedom

findings.title: subjectEnumeration.universe (CanonicalIdentifier) has no published binding to the 64-hex universe H-identity
findings.plausibleChoiceA: the domain-set member name (native.semantic-universe.typescript.v2 | .rust.v2 | .syntax.v2), denoting the set of Plan-bound universes of that domain
findings.evidenceAgainstB: CanonicalIdentifier requires a leading [a-z]; roughly ten of sixteen possible digests are unrepresentable. A per-Run digest in a policy is also not portable across snapshots.
findings.residualAmbiguityUnderA: multi-universe Runs are explicitly non-hypothetical (native-evidence.md 314-323); union vs per-universe enumeration is unpublished
findings.discriminatingExample: Run binds U_ts and U_syn, each with a complete file@enumerated scope over a.ts. Union -> one subject; per-universe -> two evaluations; digest -> whichever was pasted. Three different predicateProofs arrays, three different proof2.

findings.title: Subject selection source, subjectKind vocabulary mapping, export referent and glob applicability are all unpublished
subDefects: which scopes' subjects are unioned is unpublished (all scopes of the kind vs only scopes of relations named by the rule's atoms)
DSL {file,symbol,export,package} vs registry {source-path,symbol,package-name}: no mapping; export names no relation, no scope and no retained field, so it is a schema-valid vacuous pass today
LogicalPath globs over opaque SubjectIdV1 subjects have no defined semantics; subjectKindLaw states symbol-to-file attribution is NOT re-derivable
no rule forces atom relation subjectKind to agree with the rule subjectKind, so subjectKind:file + relation:calls yields none==true, a fabricated universal negative

findings.title: No published mechanism binds an atom to the CURRENT enumerated subject, and subjectOf(fact) is undefined
findings.detail: FieldFilter compares to a literal value only; there is no $subject placeholder and no eq-subject comparator, and no prose states implicit per-subject restriction. Separately, no registry row publishes which payload field carries the subject; the only published binding is relations.file.coverageTotality.pathField, introduced for the totality law.
findings.discriminatingExample: Rule subjectKind:file, emitWhen {exists, file, enumerated, filters:[]} over 100 files. Implicit binding -> per-file values and findings only where a file fact exists. No binding -> 100 identical true proofs and 100 findings. Both satisfy every published sentence; verdict differs.

findings.title: Imported-evidence atoms cannot be witnessed: predicate-witness is closed with fact2-only matchingFactIds
findings.detail: Section 4's 'witness facts must be exactly those selected' and 'Counts count distinct selected fact IDs' are unsatisfiable for exists/count-at-most over runtime-observation or history-change. Requires typed change.

findings.title: Disabled rules: no published evaluation behavior
findings.detail: enabled exists only in PolicyDocumentV1 while the projection law places every rule in RuleProgramV1. Skip-entirely vs evaluate-then-suppress produce different predicateProofs sets and different proof2.

findings.title: Completeness scope selection for none / count-at-most / all-covered is unpublished
findings.detail: An atom carries no universe and its rung is a lower bound, while a scope carries exactly one rung. Complete-at-exactly-k vs complete-at-every-rung->=k give different 'none' results on any two-rung relation.

findings.title: Finding identity is not recomputable from the retained closure
findings.detail: subjectKey requires language, kind, logicalPath, qualifiedName, discriminator. From a retained subject string only logicalPath is derivable, and only for source-path subjects. No retained record holds subject-adapter output and no ProofInputRef domain can name one, so section 4's 'recomputes finding fingerprints' is not discharge-able. Native-evidence openly calls the token projection a named qualification task.

findings.title: Verdict law, waiver retention and the two disagreeing Verdict enums
findings.detail: gateSeverityAtLeast has no published interaction with Rule.gate. Whether a waived finding remains in proof.findingIds is unstated and changes proof2. The four-valued surface Verdict and the three-valued sealed verdict are unrelated by any published sentence. Symbol findings have no path-form waiver.

findings.title: Section 4 misnames the artifact that carries subject enumeration
findings.detail: Section 4 says 'The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration'. RuleProgramV1 contains no subjectEnumeration, severity, gate, evidenceUse or messageCode; those live in PolicyDocumentV1, which is already a legal ProofInputRef.domain.

corrections.law: subjectEnumeration.universe and FieldFilter{field:'universe'}.value are domain-set member names from identity-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-digest-domains/domainSets/native-semantic-universe; an unlisted name refuses (POLICY.UNKNOWN_UNIVERSE). The name denotes U(rule) = every Plan-bound universe H-identity of that domain; a fact matches on sourceUniverse in U(rule).
corrections.unresolvedChoice: union subjects across U by byte equality (RECOMMENDED, because predicateProofs[].subjectId is bare Text and cannot carry a universe discriminator without an invented encoding that would propagate into waivers and fingerprints) vs per-universe evaluation

corrections.kind: registry rows + law + one enum narrowing
corrections.law: Add per-relation policySubjectKind (source-path->file, package-name->package, symbol->symbol) and subjectField to x-opensip-relation-registry. Subject set = union of subjects over subject-scopes reachable from Plan-selected views with sourceUniverse in U(rule) and matching policySubjectKind, then include/exclude. Withdraw 'export' from the subjectKind enum. Globs admissible only for subjectKind:file; otherwise POLICY.SUBJECT_GLOB_NOT_APPLICABLE. Atom relation policySubjectKind must equal the rule subjectKind else POLICY.ATOM_SUBJECT_KIND_MISMATCH.

Every atom is implicitly restricted to the current enumerated subject: fact f matches for subject s iff payload(f)[subjectField(relation(f))] == s AND relation, rung (>=), universe and all filters hold. FieldFilter{field:'subject'} is an additional constraint on that same projected value, never the binding.

corrections.kind: registry rows + law + one enum narrowing
corrections.law: Add targetFieldByRung per relation, defined as exactly the field that rung's existing rungs.required entry names. universe binds fact.sourceUniverse. subjectKind resolves through policySubjectKind. Withdraw targetKind. observability admissible only on runtime-observation atoms. Filters conjoin in admitted order. A rung-forbidden field projects absent -> filter FALSE (never indeterminate), because rungs.forbidden makes the absence a published certainty. glob/prefix require a path-shaped projected value and refuse on SubjectIdV1.

Refuse none, count-at-most and all-covered over evidence relations at policy admission (section 4 already holds that runtime unhit never supplies universal static completeness, so those could never be true and are today undecidable rather than refused). For the surviving exists, add a required matchingImportSubjects member to predicate-witness with items {importId (import2), subjectIndex}, x-opensip-order canonical-set; RuntimePayloadV1.subjects is an ordered array with a declared sort so an index is a stable deterministic address needing no new identity domain. Bind an import atom's subject to RuntimeSubject.path / HistorySubject.path, admissible only under subjectKind:file; do NOT map RuntimeSubject.symbol to SubjectIdV1.
corrections.cost: predicate-witness schemaVersion 2->3 changes every witness digest and therefore every proof2/seal2/run2; section 3 already requires a new identifier major and reviewed migration for exactly this.

corrections.law: enabled=false means no subject enumerated, no predicate proof, no finding. The rule stays in RuleProgramV1 (the projection law forbids dropping it) and stays ladder-checked, so toggling a rule does not change ruleProgramDigest.

An atom over relation R at rung k for subject s is COMPLETE iff, for EVERY rung of R's ladder with index >= k, some subject-scope reachable from this predicate's inputRefs carries that rung, a universe in U(rule), contains s, and its Coverage entry has coverage==complete and the section-4-required resolution/closed-world completeness. Empty set is INDETERMINATE, never complete. Those scopes are exactly predicateProofs[].scopeIds and those Coverage ids exactly predicate-witness.coverageIds, so the computation replays from retained bytes.
corrections.rationale: 'every rung >= k' rather than 'exactly k' because the match set spans those rungs; the weaker reading asserts a negative over unexamined rungs.

corrections.law: Law part: omitted Rule.messageCode yields messageCode = ruleId; DSL v1 emits finding-parameters.parameters = {} (fixing parameterDigest); a (ruleId, subjectPath) waiver matches only source-path subjects and a symbol finding is waivable only by fingerprint. Typed part: register a subject-descriptor record {schemaVersion:2, scopeId, subject, language, kind, logicalPath, qualifiedName, signatureTokens[]} produced by the same enumerator closure that mints subject-scope, plus a subject-descriptor member on ProofInputRef.domain.
corrections.ownershipCaveat: This may belong to the native contract's already-named token-projection qualification task rather than to this correction; a correction author should confirm ownership before writing it.

corrections.law: A finding is gating iff rule.gate AND rank(rule.severity) >= rank(policy.gateSeverityAtLeast) over note<warning<error. verdict = fail if any gating finding is unwaived; else indeterminate if any gating rule carried an indeterminate required predicate; else pass. Waived findings REMAIN in proof.findingIds (they are evidence) and are excluded only from gating. proof-bundle / evaluation-seal / policy-derivation verdicts stay three-valued; common#/$defs/Verdict.advisory is a surface projection of a pass carrying unwaived non-gating findings and is never sealed.

limits: Read scope was the sections named above, not the full 258 KB native-evidence contract, IMPLEMENTATION-FREEZE.md or IMPLEMENTER-BLUEPRINT.md. Every occurrence of subjectEnumeration, gateSeverityAtLeast and the FieldFilter vocabulary across the non-review tree was searched and no binding law was found, but a law could in principle sit in an unread region.
No prior review, author response or review directory was read; the passed architecture review was not treated as an oracle.
No claim of replay is made from schema or hash checks alone; every finding is stated as a selection-semantics gap with a concrete two-reading discriminator.
Unresolved design choices deliberately left to the correction author: per-universe vs union enumeration (C1), and ownership of the subject-descriptor record (C8).
